before.text: Fifty years of a molecular moat no competitor could cross. Kingsport acetate, emulsion science nobody could replicate, six thousand patents. Discoverer XIV in August 1960: more Soviet territory on one roll than every U-2 flight combined, snatched out of the sky over the Pacific. Film that out-resolved its own lenses. And the margins were so extraordinary that every digital move was self-harm on the balance sheet, which made renting rather than building the rational choice for roughly twenty years.

before.text: **The company ran for another eighty years on his instructions, and this is the part that has been erased.** Tennessee Eastman operated the Y-12 plant at Oak Ridge from 1943 to 1947 and enriched the uranium for Hiroshima. Kodak made the film for America's first spy satellites, whose capsules came back out of orbit to be caught in midair by aircraft trailing hooks, and built the cameras for the programs that followed. In August 1966 a Kodak system orbiting the moon developed its own film on board, scanned the negatives, and radioed home the first photograph of the Earth. At its peak Kodak held ninety percent of the American film market and was the fourth most valuable brand on the planet. It is now a slide in a deck about incumbents who fail to adapt.
